newsitem.title: USA: Signet to sell 39 branches, take charge, cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: Signet to sell 39 branches, take charge, cut jobs.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp. said Tuesday it would sell 39 branches and take a $57 million charge as part of a broad restructuring aimed at cutting costs and boosting profits.
The branch sale will result in a loss of 165 jobs, bringing the net job loss under the restructuring, first announced last October, to 327, or about 7 percent of its total work force.
The company, one of the oldest banks in the United States, said the moves would add $10 million to revenues and reduce expenses by $58 million, or 72 cents a share, by the end of 1998.
The Richmond, Va.-based banking company said that in addition to the pretax charge, to be taken in the second quarter, it would buy back up to 5 percent of its stock by the end of the year.
The company did not give estimates for its earnings or revenues for the quarter, and a spokeswoman declined to make projections.
Investors showed little reaction to the announcements, and Signet stock was unchanged at $33.50 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
After the changes are completed over the next 18 months, the company will "achieve significantly increased profitability," Chairman Malcom McDonald said in a statement.

Signet said the branches to be sold are in southwest and northern Virginia and the Eastern Shore of Virginia and Maryland. It said it expects to receive a significant premium in connection with the sale.
The company has about 233 branches in total and employed about 4,800 people at the end of 1996.

While 1,135 positions have been eliminated since October, it said 808 positions were reduced without layoffs through a hiring freeze, voluntary separations, attrition and the proposed sale of branches.
In addition to selling 39 branches, the company has previously said it would close six other branches.
Signet traces its roots back to 1795 in Maryland and says it is the eighth-oldest bank in the country.
